title: Workflow idea record
description: One workflow or broadcast this project does not have yet and arguably should, recorded so the idea can be judged before anyone builds a review surface for it. Subject is `idea:<slug>`.

idea_schema_version.description: Definition version. Charts filter on it, so bump it when a field's meaning changes.

idea_kind.description: A workflow fires per person on a trigger. A broadcast goes to an audience once.

idea_title.description: What a person would name this workflow in the list.

value_tier.description: How close the goal event is to money. `revenue`: the goal is a payment, purchase, subscription or recovered payment. `activation`: the goal is the first use that predicts paying. `retention`: the goal is a returning or reactivated user. `engagement`: anything else. Ideas rank by this tier first.

audience.description: Who it reaches, in terms this project can filter on: an event, a property, a cohort, a group. Not a persona.

trigger_kind.description: What starts it. `event` fires per person, `schedule` on a cadence, `batch` over an audience once.

trigger_name.description: The project's own event or action name, copied exactly, or the cadence for a schedule. For an event trigger it is the moment the send is timed from, so it must be an event the project already records.

trigger_verified_count.description: Times this event fired in the project over the window, read from the project before naming it. Required for an event trigger: an event you cannot count does not exist here, and the idea is not recordable.

goal_event.description: The project's own event that shows the message worked, copied exactly: the purchase, the subscription, the first successful use. The workflow exits a person who reaches it, and the outcome is measured on it.

goal_verified_count.description: Times the goal event fired over the window. Required with a goal event, for the same reason as `trigger_verified_count`.

baseline_conversion_rate.description: Share of `reach_people` who reached the goal event at any point after the trigger within `window_days`, with no message. It includes people who convert after `delay_hours`, so it is the rate a workflow has to beat.

message_outline.description: What the message says and what it asks the reader to do. Concrete enough to judge, not a finished draft.

subject_line.description: The subject line or push title of the first message, written for this project's product and in its users' language.

channel.description: The channel the message goes out on. Only a channel this project can reach its people on: email needs an email address on the person.

delay_hours.description: Hours between the trigger and the first message. Long enough for most people who will reach the goal unprompted to do so, read from how long it takes them.

message_count.description: Messages per person in the sequence, each skipped once the person reaches the goal event.

reach_people.description: Distinct people who hit the trigger over the window.

audience_people.description: Of `reach_people`, those who did not reach the goal event within the delay: the people the first message would actually go to.

reachable_people.description: Of `audience_people`, those the channel can reach (an email address on the person, for email). Under 50 the idea costs more to review than it can return, so it is not recordable.

estimated_monthly_sends.description: `reachable_people` scaled to 30 days, times `message_count`. An upper bound: later messages go only to people still short of the goal.

window_days.description: Days the reach was measured over.

existing_coverage.description: Whether a live workflow already messages this audience at this moment. `partial` means one exists but misses the moment or the audience.

covered_by.description: When coverage is `partial`: the id of the live workflow that covers it, or the event that shows another messaging tool already sends it.

confidence.description: How sure the scout is that this is worth building, given value tier, reachable audience, coverage and how cleanly the trigger and goal read.

why_now.description: What in the data makes this worth doing now rather than any other week. Every number here matches a field above.
